title: New ECAs: 0.10% sulphur in the Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea from 1 March 2027
description: The Canadian Arctic and the Norwegian Sea became Emission Control Areas under MARPOL Annex VI on 1 March 2026. The 0.10% sulphur limit applies there from 1 March 2027. What changed, who is affected and what the ship must do.

source.title: New Emission Control Areas: Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea (resolution MEPC.392(82))
IMO New Emissions Control Areas for Mediterranean Sea, Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea

script: From the 1st of March 2027, two more sea areas will demand 0.10% sulphur fuel. Is your ship ready? What changed? The Canadian Arctic and the Norwegian Sea are now Emission Control Areas under MARPOL Annex VI, in force since the 1st of March 2026. Why? Emission Control Areas cut sulphur oxides, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from ship exhaust. When? The nitrogen oxide Tier III rules already apply to newer ships, depending on their build dates. The sulphur limit follows twelve months later, on the 1st of March 2027. Who is affected? Every ship operating there. Fuel must not exceed 0.10% sulphur, unless an approved equivalent such as an exhaust gas cleaning system is used. What must the ship do? Plot the ECA limits in your passage plan. Secure compliant fuel early. Follow your written fuel changeover procedure, and log the changeover with date, time, position and tank volumes. Stay updated with the maritime industry. Follow HeyMariner.
